Evidence: the section's premise (one field list written three times) does not hold. The three surfaces differ deliberately -- HandlesRequestBuilder omits Request and TelemetryCorrelation, and InferenceRequest has no maxTokens/streaming fields at all. Those two are builder state that create() folds into options via override(), which skips nulls and applies AFTER the caller's options. Net effect, measured: the builder (and therefore the Inference facade) makes withStreaming/withMaxTokens win over a conflicting withOptions key REGARDLESS of call order, whereas InferenceRequest's own withers are last-writer-wins. Part B would have flipped public behaviour from order-independent to order-dependent while leaving every signature byte-identical -- passing a signature-level 'public API unchanged' check while breaking the observable contract. This also resolves the plan's own flagged tension: the internal buffering IS the precedence rule, so keeping the behaviour requires keeping a builder.

The alternative fails too: generating forwarders means __call() (loses compile-time arg checking, needs an @method block that is a fourth copy), and exposing the builder directly changes the public API the acceptance criteria protect.

Landed instead: packages/polyglot/tests/Unit/Inference/InferenceOptionPrecedenceTest.php (5 tests) pinning the precedence, which was previously untested -- the existing builder test sets each field once, where both semantics agree.
